desc: PM Carney made an official visit to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, from July 8th to July 10th, marking the first visit by a Canadian prime minister to the kingdom in 26 years.[3][5][8] On July 9th, he was greeted at the Royal Palace by Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, held a bilateral meeting and lunch with him, and participated in a signing ceremony.[3] He also delivered remarks and took part in a Saudi Arabia-Canada Investment Forum event in Jeddah, where Canada and Saudi Arabia announced 13 new commercial agreements and MOUs worth over C$1 billion, covering areas including health technology, mining, infrastructure, and defence.[1][8] The two sides also announced work toward a Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement by the end of 2027, launched negotiations on a double-taxation agreement, and established a foreign minister-level Canada-Saudi Arabia Coordination Council.[8]
summary: PM Carney visited Jeddah from July 8th to July 10th for a high-level meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, a signing ceremony, and the Saudi Arabia-Canada Investment Forum, where the two countries announced more than C$1 billion in new commercial agreements.
